parameters.content:
## [Jev Real Case 5/5] Every Jev action in one operations console
### How it works
One webhook takes every request. Normalize Ops Request keeps the run id, requester
text and destination, then the Request Text Usable? guard marks empty text and emails
ops. Usable text goes to Jev Classify Request Type (fixed categories, threshold 0.6,
uncertain handling Send to Needs Review Output): four work types plus a review output.
Each output owns a route Set and a Jev operation: Ask Questions for vendor invoice
fields, Score for incident urgency, Check for a report and for an external share. Each
lane logs a Jev Console row, then pages a human or emails the desk. A Monday schedule
counts runs per route and emails the brief.
### Setup
1. Point your operations form at the Ops Request Intake webhook (POST).
2. Attach the Jev (TypeSafe) API, Sheets, Gmail, Telegram and OpenAI credentials.
3. Replace the placeholder addresses and the Telegram chat id with your own.
4. Tune the Jev operations, route Set owners and the digest recipient.
### Customization
Add work types, or mirror the log into Slack or Linear.

### Request intake and classify
The Ops Request Intake webhook normalises the payload, the Request Text Usable? guard bounces empty text to the console mailbox, and Jev Classify Request Type sorts every usable request into four work types plus a needs review output.

### Jev action lanes
Every classify output owns a route Set, one Jev operation and one row in the Jev Console tab. Urgent outcomes page a human on Telegram, desk acknowledgements go out by Gmail, and unclear requests wait for a senior operator.

### Weekly console digest
Every Monday at 09:00 the schedule trigger reads the Jev Console tab, counts runs per route, asks the agent for a short brief and emails it to the ops inbox.

### One workflow, four Jev operations
Classify picks the work type, Ask Questions reads the vendor invoice fields, Score rates incident urgency and Check tests text for personal data. Four operations, four lanes, one console log.
